notes:
Nissan Leaf, first generation (ZE0, 2010 to 2017) and its AZE0 update, on the Car-CAN pair of the diagnostic socket (pins 6 and 14, 11-bit identifiers, 500 kbit/s). The EV-CAN and AV-CAN buses are not on the socket's CAN pins, so units that sit only there are not listed.

Every address is a fact transcribed from open diagnostic-tool sources; no signal definition is copied. Treat every row as unconfirmed until `obd-read probe` shows the unit answering. The sources disagree about the response offset, so each unit names its own response identifier: 0x20 above the request for 0x740, 0x743, 0x744, 0x745, 0x79B and 0x79D, 3 for the charger (0x797 to 0x79A), 8 for 0x784, 1 for 0x792.

Service is per unit. The battery controller (0x79B) is read with service 21 (local identifier, one byte) in both OVMS and OBDb; the charger (0x797) is read with service 22 (two-byte identifier) in OBDb, though OVMS also reads its VIN with service 21 and identifier 0x81. The units 0x745, 0x784, 0x792 and 0x79D are named only in an OVMS source comment as other address pairs, with no service evidence; they carry the profile's service 22 as a placeholder.

A vendor handout lists a Nissan secure gateway from 2020, which is not documented in any source here; a unit that stays silent on a newer car is reported as no response, not as a fault. The Leaf of the second generation (ZE1) is not covered: OVMS says its OBD port cannot be used reliably because the gateway powers down with the car.

Session caveat: no source shows a Leaf, Qashqai, Juke or X-Trail unit accepting the session this profile opens. opendbc sends 10 81 and then 21 83 to Nissan units only to fingerprint their software version, and OBDb's Leaf file sets diagnosticLevel C0, which the guard does not allow, so the profile does not use it. Session 0x81 (KWP2000) and 0x01 (UDS) are guard-permitted values chosen from that evidence and are unconfirmed; confirming them on a real car is tracked in https://github.com/Mearman/obd/issues/70.
name: nissan-leaf
description: Nissan Leaf ZE0 and AZE0 (2010 to 2017), Car-CAN

vin.source: The WMIs are the makers' car and SUV identifiers in the world manufacturer identifier table of the Wikipedia article Vehicle identification number, which cites the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt manufacturer list SV 3.2 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number, archived https://web.archive.org/web/20261102120229/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number). A WMI names the maker and plant, not the model, so a match only says the car is of a make this profile covers.
